newsitem.title: USA: Baxter sees 1997 low double-digit growth.
newsitem.headline: Baxter sees 1997 low double-digit growth.

text.p: Baxter International Inc said it expects 1997 net income to grow in the low double digit range and sees operational cash flow of at least $300 million, excluding litigation, after investing about $1 billion in research and development and capital expenses.

The healthcare products concern on Wednesday reported first-quarter net income from continuing operations of $0.55 per share, up eight percent from the year-ago period and in line with the First Call consensus Wall Street estimate.
"We are on track to meet our financial commitments for the full year," said chief financial officer Harry Kraemer.
Kraemer was recently appointed president of Baxter and is acting as chief financial officer until a replacement can be found, the company said.
Baxter's first-quarter sales totaled $1.44 billion, an increase of 11 percent over $1.30 billion a year ago.

Without the impact of a stronger U.S. dollar, sales increased 13 percent. Sales outside the United States grew 17 percent, to $765 million, representing 53 percent of Baxter's total sales in the first quarter, the company said.
"We experienced strong sales growth in two of our fastest growing markets -- Latin America and Asia," Kraemer said.
"We expect stronger sales growth for the remainder of 1997," he said.
Shares in Baxter were off 1/8 to 46-3/4.
